STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple sitting on a white paper plate, photographed from directly above. It is not really a meal; it is a single piece of fruit.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white paper plate looks roughly 20 cm in diameter (side-plate size). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 = 314 cm^2. The apple's width is about 1/3 of the plate's diameter, which is consistent with a ~7-8 cm apple.

STEP 3 - Items: One red-yellow apple (whole, with stem cavity visible).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's top view covers about 0.3 x 0.3 of the plate's frame, roughly 40-45 cm^2 of the 314 cm^2 plate, so about 13% of the vessel.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly a sphere/oblate shape about 7.5 cm across and 7 cm tall, so its volume is about 200-230 ml. Using the footprint (~45 cm^2) times height (~6.5 cm) gives about 290 ml as an envelope, but the actual solid volume is closer to 200 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole apple is dense fruit, so the density is near 0.85-0.9 g/ml (whole fruit, not a cut pile). 200 ml x 0.85 ≈ 170 g. A typical medium apple weighs about 150-180 g, which agrees.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple, raw, about 52 kcal per 100 g. 170 g x 0.52 ≈ 88 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium apple at about 170 g and about 90 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The plate is only partly covered, which fits a single fruit.
